items.title: OpenAI and Cisco Releases Shirudo: An Open-Source Linux Runtime Allowing Agents to Defend Systems Without Downtime
items.description:
OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, a pre-release, BSD-licensed eBPF runtime for Linux. AI agents write signed "shields" that block exploit paths on running systems while teams test and roll out real patches.

The post
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source eBPF runtime for Linux that allows AI agents to deploy protective "shields" on running systems, enabling continuous defense against exploits without downtime. This tool is crucial as it enhances cybersecurity by providing real-time protection during the patch development process.
items.summary_detailed: OpenAI and Cisco have released Shirudo, an open-source eBPF runtime for Linux that allows AI agents to deploy "shields" to block exploit paths on running systems. This enables security teams to test and implement patches without system downtime. The broader impact could enhance real-time cybersecurity by integrating AI in a non-disruptive manner across various Linux-based systems.
items.summary_bullets:
• OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo.
• Shirudo is a BSD-licensed eBPF runtime for Linux.
• AI agents can write "shields" to block exploits.
